brief.greeting: Good morning. Your inbox just got a dose of cheaper AI and tighter kernels.

stories.headline: Asana slashes GPT-6.1 spend
stories.body: **Browser agent gets a budget makeover:** Asana’s internal tests show its GPT-6 Astra‑based agent is now 76× cheaper and 5× faster. The savings come from a new inference pipeline that trims compute waste.
stories.why: Lower inference costs let you run smarter assistants without blowing your cloud bill.

stories.headline: Linux distro patch marathon
stories.body: **Friday’s bulk patch drop:** AlmaLinux, Debian, Fedora, Mageia, Oracle, Red Hat, SUSE, and Ubuntu released updates for dozens of packages, including bind, glibc, openssl, and the kernel. It’s the usual scramble to close known exploits before they’re weaponized.
stories.why: Staying current prevents attackers from exploiting outdated libraries you already run.

stories.headline: GCC adds kernel CFI check
stories.body: **Forward‑edge control‑flow integrity lands:** Kees Cook merged a GCC feature that enforces forward‑edge CFI for the Linux kernel. The compiler now inserts checks that stop jumps to unexpected code paths, tightening runtime security.
stories.why: Hardening the kernel at compile time raises the bar for exploit developers.

quick_hits.text: **3D printing hack:** Riley turned a broken Prusa into a liquid extruder for embedded prints.
**Cert lifespan shift:** Let’s Encrypt will issue 64‑day TLS certs starting Feb 2027.
**Token trim library:** headroom reduces JSON tokens by up to 95% before LLMs see them.
**Python 3.15 release:** Adds sentinel and frozendict types, makes UTF‑8 default encoding.
**Rust‑core AI gateway:** litellm supports 100+ LLM APIs with cost tracking and guardrails.

brief.sign_off: Catch you tomorrow – same time, same place.

highlights.title: Embedded 3D Printing with Liquids on a Bricked Prusa FDM Printer
highlights.summary: Riley retrofitted a broken Prusa i3 FDM printer to extrude liquid material for embedded 3D printing.
highlights.detail: The project repurposes a printer whose hot‑end was damaged, adding a custom extrusion system that can deposit liquids while the print head moves. It demonstrates a low‑cost way to combine additive manufacturing with fluid deposition, opening possibilities for multi‑material prototypes.

highlights.title: Asana cuts model costs 76x in browser tests with GPT-6.1 Sol
highlights.summary: Asana’s browser agent using GPT-6 Astra in Codex became 76× cheaper and 5× faster in internal tests.
highlights.detail: The cost reduction stems from more efficient inference and lower token usage. Faster response times improve user experience for real‑time collaboration tools. The changes were evaluated in controlled browser benchmarks before rollout.

highlights.title: Security updates for Friday
highlights.summary: AlmaLinux, Debian, Fedora, Mageia, Oracle, Red Hat, SUSE, and Ubuntu issued security updates for dozens of packages such as bind, glibc, openssl, and the kernel.
highlights.detail: The updates address vulnerabilities disclosed in recent CVEs and are distributed through each distribution's regular update channels. Administrators should apply them promptly to keep systems protected against remote code execution and privilege‑escalation attacks.

highlights.title: [$] Adding kernel control-flow-integrity checking to GCC
highlights.summary: Kees Cook added forward‑edge control‑flow integrity checking for the Linux kernel to the GCC compiler suite.
highlights.detail: The new GCC support, presented at the 2026 GNU Tools Cauldron, enables the kernel to enforce CFI at compile time, reducing the attack surface for control‑flow hijacking. It complements existing mitigations like retpoline and eBPF‑based checks.

highlights.title: Impactful scheduling for GPU clusters
highlights.summary: A Hugging Face blog post discusses new scheduling algorithms for GPU clusters.
highlights.detail: The article outlines techniques to improve job placement and resource utilization across heterogeneous GPU farms. It compares the proposed scheduler against common FIFO and priority‑based baselines, showing modest throughput gains in synthetic workloads.

items.title: Sophos cuts threat investigation time by 96% with OpenAI Daybreak
items.summary: Sophos reduced cyber‑threat investigation time by 96% and automated 52% of MDR cases using OpenAI’s Daybreak.
items.detail: Daybreak provides a large‑language‑model assistant that triages alerts, extracts indicators, and suggests remediation steps while keeping analysts in the loop. The automation maintains compliance by flagging high‑risk actions for human review.

items.title: Model: Cactus-Compute/whistle
items.summary: Cactus‑Compute/whistle is an automatic‑speech‑recognition model with 5,558 downloads and 279 likes on Hugging Face.
items.detail: The model is optimized for low‑latency transcription on edge devices. Community feedback highlights its robustness to noisy environments, though benchmark scores are not listed.

items.title: Model: LiquidAI/d1-3B
items.summary: LiquidAI/d1-3B is an image‑to‑text model that has been downloaded 7,302 times and received 243 likes.
items.detail: At 3 B parameters, the model balances capability and compute cost, making it suitable for research prototypes. Users note good performance on captioning tasks despite limited fine‑tuning data.

items.title: Model: Qwen/Qwen-Image-2.1-Turbo
items.summary: Qwen‑Image‑2.1‑Turbo is a text‑to‑image model on Hugging Face with 358 likes.
items.detail: The Turbo variant offers faster generation than its predecessor while preserving image quality. It is frequently used in creative workflows, though download statistics were not disclosed.

items.title: Let's Encrypt moving to 64-day certificate lifetimes in 2027
items.summary: Let's Encrypt will issue 64‑day TLS certificates starting February 10 2027, with the final 90‑day cert expiring May 11 2027.
items.detail: This change is the second phase of a plan to shorten certificate lifetimes, following a 2025 announcement to move to 45‑day certs in 2028. Existing certificates remain valid; only newly issued or renewed ones will have the shorter validity.

items.title: Python 3.15 released
items.summary: Python 3.15 has been released, adding sentinel and frozendict built‑in types and making UTF‑8 the default source encoding.
items.detail: The release also includes experimental JIT compiler improvements and new package start‑up configuration files. Developers can review the full changelog for additional performance tweaks and deprecations.

items.title: [$] The state of systemd: 2026 edition
items.summary: At the 2026 All Systems Go! conference, systemd maintainers presented the project's yearly status and discussed its size, health, and future direction.
items.detail: The session covered recent feature additions, bug‑fix trends, and clarified that systemd is not intended to replace Kubernetes. A follow‑up round‑table addressed community questions about scalability and integration.

items.title: headroomlabs-ai/headroom
items.summary: headroomlabs-ai/headroom is a Python library that compresses tool outputs, logs, files, and RAG chunks before they reach LLMs, achieving 20% token reduction for coding agents and 60‑95% for JSON while preserving answers.
items.detail: The library can be used as a proxy or MCP server, integrating seamlessly into existing pipelines. It targets token cost savings without altering LLM output quality, making it useful for cost‑sensitive applications.

items.title: BerriAI/litellm
items.summary: BerriAI/litellm provides a Rust‑core AI gateway with a Python SDK that supports over 100 LLM APIs in OpenAI format, adding cost tracking, guardrails, load balancing, and logging.
items.detail: The gateway unifies disparate provider interfaces, enabling developers to switch backends without code changes. Features like guardrails and load balancing help manage reliability and compliance in production deployments.

items.title: DamRsn/NeuralNote
items.summary: DamRsn/NeuralNote is a C++ audio plugin that transcribes audio to MIDI using deep‑learning models.
items.detail: The plugin can be integrated into digital audio workstations, allowing real‑time conversion of recorded performances into MIDI data for further editing or synthesis. It leverages neural networks to improve transcription accuracy over traditional rule‑based methods.

items.title: Robbyant/lingbot-map
items.summary: Robbyant/lingbot-map introduces LingBot-Map, a Geometric Context Transformer for streaming 3D reconstruction, and is a Best Paper Award candidate at ECCV 2026.
items.detail: The model processes incoming visual data to build 3D maps in real time, improving geometric consistency compared to prior batch methods. Its transformer architecture enables better context integration across frames.

items.title: bojieli/ai-agent-book
items.summary: bojieli/ai-agent-book is the open‑source repository for the Chinese book "深入理解 AI Agent：设计原理与工程实践", containing the full text, PDF, and chapter‑specific code.
